key_insight: Rust ownership plus Aeneas-to-Lean extraction lets the team verify production cryptographic code at scale without reasoning about pointer aliasing and liveness.
engineering_relevance: The approach shows that verified cryptographic software can remain fast, portable, and maintainable enough for real deployment on x86-64 and ARM.
method: Extract Rust code into a pure Lean model with Aeneas.
Use Lean tactics and libraries to prove safety, panic-freedom, and functional correctness.
Apply AI agents to draft proofs and help formalize standards and platform intrinsics, with Lean kernel checking the results.
evidence_signal: The paper reports a 237 KLOC Lean development verifying 16.7 KLOC of Rust code for post-quantum cipher suites across x86-64 and ARM, including SHA-3 and ML-KEM implementations.
watch_item: Verification still depends on expert review for cryptographic standards, intrinsic semantics, and other platform-specific details that automation cannot fully resolve.
paper_title: Scaling Verification of Cryptographic Software with Aeneas, Rust, and Lean
